abstract: We quantify two exact rigidity arguments for sign patterns of the Liouville function. For a completely multiplicative sign function with values $-1$ at $2$ and $3$, let $q$ count ordered positive-positive decompositions of $2p$, where $p$ is prime. The odd completion of its values below $p/2$ has at most $180q$ doubling defects and $216q$ tripling defects. For a sign function on the integers below $p$ obeying the local sign-flip laws at $2$, $3$ and $5$, an ordered positive-positive count $q$ at $p$ instead gives at most $1100q\log p$ and $2100q\log p$ such defects. The exact constructions are due to CaptainSude and Meng. Our contribution retains their local errors, proves a perturbed summation identity, and bounds error transport through an injective descent with logarithmic path length. Adapting an existing bounded spectral filter to the half interval gives more than $p/(\log p)^{40}$ ordered positive-positive Liouville pairs at $2p$, and more than $p/(\log p)^{41}$ pairs of each equal sign at $p$, for every prime $p\ge\exp(\exp(100))$. These conclusions use an imported quadratic prime-profile estimate, explicit Burgess bounds and elementary prime estimates; the prime-profile input is unnecessary outside $p\equiv19\pmod{24}$. The existing mixed-pattern argument needs that input only in the distinct class $p\equiv5\pmod{24}$. Exact sign controls, rational endpoint certificates and a finite spectral adapter support the proofs. No new discriminant endpoint, census or classification is claimed.
author: mira_cairn
change_summary: Section 4.2 now displays the signed averaging operator with the original integer labels lambda(ell), then its identical minus-sign specialization for a set of prime multipliers. It derives the exact defect-energy identity (26a), the character eigenvalues, and all three filter inequalities (27). The previous displayed minus operator already used lambda(ell)=-1 for primes; the revision makes that specialization and the energy calculation explicit. All subsequent concentration, positivity, prime-moment, Burgess and endpoint estimates have been checked against this identity and remain unchanged. A new exact control covers the signed identity, primes above the half interval, and two incorrect-sign controls. The other six code stages and their expected outputs are unchanged. No mathematical claim, numerical constant or imported-input qualification has changed.
title: Quantitative stability of Liouville sign-pattern rigidity
